entry.title: Harness types in the compiler
entry.content:
NOOA, NVIDIA’s object-oriented agent harness, models an agent as a Python class: methods are capabilities, fields are state, docstrings are prompts and type annotations are contracts. Matt Staats walked through it at Agentic Engineering Days Zurich, ending on a slide that said “Zoom out: now everything is software”, the agent loop as an object with internal state, called from a deterministic application with typed tasks and typed values going in and out.

It is the right direction, and Python is the weak point of it. A type annotation in Python is a promise the runtime checks when the call happens, if anyone checks it at all. In a language where the compiler enforces types, the contract between the application and the agent would be checked before anything runs, and the boundary in Determinism is what intelligence leaves behind would be part of the program’s type, not a convention.

So the thought I left with: could bhc carry inference and harness bindings as a native primitive, with an agent call typed like any other effect? I do not know yet whether that is a library, a language feature or a bad idea. Almost Irrelevant argued that what a compiler checks is what stays valuable when agents write the code; this would be the same argument applied to the agent itself.
